subject: Telemetry anomaly and request for IRP / evidence preservation
messages:
From: Elaine Zhao <elaine.zhao@finserve.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finserve.com
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry anomaly — immediate preservation & IRP evidence checklist

Hi Logan / Marissa,

We observed a telemetry spike and a small set of unusual requests against our Redwood deployment (customer tenant id: finserve-prod-23) between 02:13–02:19 UTC today. Initial triage shows anomalous token usage and a handful of requests that returned unexpected PII in the response payload (snippets withheld).

Can you please:
- Confirm Redwood will preserve all relevant logs and request/response payloads for the window above (transaction logs, request ids, audit trails, and any service-level traces).
- Provide your incident response plan (IRP) stub and a list of artifacts you can produce for SOC 2 / SIG review (redaction options welcome).
- Let us know expected timelines for an initial artifact handover and an internal postmortem.

FinServe legal (cc'ed) requests we treat this as an incident for now and preserve evidence. We need the following as soon as possible: a preservation acknowledgement, a copy of the IRP, and an index of logs you will share.

Thanks — we appreciate a quick acknowledgement.

Elaine Zhao
Director, Security Operations
FinServe Inc.

Attachments: none
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhao <elaine.zhao@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tom Reddick <tom.reddick@legalco.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 08:27:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry anomaly — immediate preservation & IRP evidence checklist

Elaine — thanks for the flag and for the detail. We are treating this as an active incident. Short answers up front: yes, we will preserve all request/response logs, service traces, and audit events for the timeframe you called out.

What we'll produce in the first handover (T+4 hours target):
- Preservation acknowledgement (see attached stub).
- A redacted log bundle covering 2028-09-05T02:00:00Z to 2028-09-05T02:30:00Z (initial snapshot).
- An index of artifacts and a short IRP summary (what we will follow operationally).

Can you confirm whether FinServe requires:
- Full payloads (unredacted) or redacted extracts?
- Any specific retention window beyond our default 90 days?

We have initiated an internal containment review and routed a follow-up to the forensics team (cc: Karthik). I will add a link to our Confluence IRP and will provide a presigned share for the redacted logs. If you prefer an encrypted SFTP handoff, we can do that as well.

Logan Wright
Group Product Manager, Trust & Privacy
Redwood Inference

—Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhao <elaine.zhao@finserve.com>, Tom Reddick <tom.reddick@legalco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: redwood incident SUP-4872 (redacted postmortem & next steps)

Elaine / Tom —

Attached is the redacted postmortem for incident SUP-4872 and the evidence index you requested. Summary highlights:

Root cause (high level): transient misconfiguration in a cache key derivation function led to rare duplication of request identifiers under a small set of tenant routing conditions. That duplication caused an internal cache hit to return a response previously associated with a different request under an edge condition. There is no evidence of bulk data exfiltration; affected responses were limited and our review shows 12 unique responses with potentially sensitive snippets.

Actions taken (short term):
- Immediate cache invalidation for affected nodes and rollback of the faulty key derivation change.
- Preserved full debug traces and request/response logs (redacted copies attached and available via presigned link).
- Notified downstream teams and rotated a small set of ephemeral keys as a precaution.

Planned long-term mitigations:
- Add a guardrail in the cache key path to prevent key collisions and improve deterministic hashing.
- Expand unit and integration tests for multi-tenant routing edge cases.
- Update our IRP runbook to include a checklist for payload redaction and customer notification timelines.

We appreciate FinServe's collaboration on evidence acceptability and redaction scope. As discussed with legal, we are prepared to provide additional forensic support for your internal review; please confirm if you want the unredacted artifacts under an appropriate NDA / data sharing agreement.

Links & artifacts:
- Redacted postmortem: https://s3-presigned.example.com/finserve/redacted-logs?expires=2028-09-19
- Confluence IRP page: https://redwood-confluence.internal/IRP/finserve-4872
- Jira ticket: JIRA-SUP-4872

We will follow up with an internal retrospective and a scheduled tabletop drill to validate the new guardrail. If you need a formal SOC 2 / SIG crosswalk for the artifacts we provided, Marissa will share the mapping doc.

Thanks — please reach out with any questions or if you need additional artifact formats.

Logan Wright
Group Product Manager, Trust & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-redacted.pdf (attachment stub), evidence-index.csv (attachment stub)
